title: Why Airplane Windows Have Tiny Holes

lines.text: Have you ever noticed that tiny pinhole at the bottom of airplane windows?
Most passengers assume it's a crack or manufacturing defect,
but without it, cabin pressure would shatter the window at 35,000 feet.
In reality, the window is an architectural stack of three acrylic panes.
The middle pane contains a tiny bleed valve, venting air between the chambers.
This self-balances the pressure, routing all stress directly to the outer hull.
Beneath the seal, dry air circulates through a moisture-wicking channel,
maintaining four atmospheres of safety with a hole just two millimeters wide.
So that tiny hole holds the cabin safe, while you fly smoothly through the clouds.
